## Natural history notes

A small grass-veneer moth characterized by narrow straw-colored to pale yellowish wings with mottled brown markings and fine longitudinal lines that help it blend into dry grasses. In Florida, it is most likely found in open grassy habitats such as prairies, pine flatwoods, roadsides, fields, lawns, and marsh edges where grasses are available. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars are associated with grasses and may feed near the base or roots, helping move grass biomass into the broader food web for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
